subtype: Approach: rehearsing a light reply to avoid a fight [Thinking]
passage: Only five minutes of lunch were left, the corridor was loud, and Akash, a friend of Mridul's, was already walking towards Mridul with his maths notebook open. Mridul knew what was coming. He had rehearsed on the stairs: not "That is cheating", which would sound like a lecture, but something about himself. "Akash, I do not want trouble with Ma'am. Sorry, I cannot." He had said it in his head twice. When Akash reached him and asked for the homework answers, Mridul swallowed, then said it aloud. Akash shrugged, a little stiff. "Okay, fine." No sulking. Mridul's shoulders dropped. It had been easier than he feared, mostly because he had made it about himself.

qa.q: What reason did Mridul plan to give?
qa.a: He planned to say he did not want trouble with Ma'am.

qa.q: Why did Mridul choose that reason instead of calling it cheating?
qa.a: He worried a lecture would upset Akash and wanted to refuse without judging his friend.

qa.q: What could Mridul offer along with the refusal?
qa.a: Offer to explain the method after class, because it helps Akash without breaking the rules.

qa.q: How might Akash have felt at the refusal?
qa.a: Slightly stiff or disappointed but not insulted, since he shrugged and said okay without sulking.

grounding: A boy prepares a refusal that sounds about himself, not a judgement on his friend, so it is easier to accept.

subtype: Approach: rehearsing a light reply to avoid a fight [Thinking]
passage: On the auto ride to school in Pune, Pradeep went over it in his head. Yesterday Sarita had hinted she'd ask to copy his English homework today, like last week. Last week he'd said, "That's cheating," and she'd sulked for two days. "That made it about her," he thought. "As if I was calling her a cheat." What if he made it about himself instead? He practised under his breath: "Sorry, I can't. Ma'am compared my book with Rohan's last time, and I really don't want any trouble." It was true, and it didn't point at her at all. At the gate Sarita came up. "Pradeep, English?" He said his line. She shrugged. "Okay, fair." And she walked with him to class, chatting about cricket.

qa.q: How long did Sarita sulk last week?
What was Pradeep thinking as he rehearsed?
qa.a: He was worried about hurting Sarita again and wanted a refusal that didn't sound like judging her.

qa.q: What else could Pradeep offer Sarita?
qa.a: To go over the English homework with her at lunch, so she isn't left stuck.

qa.q: How does Sarita react this time?
qa.a: Sarita shrugs, says 'Okay, fair', and walks with him chatting about cricket.

grounding: A boy prepares a refusal about his own wish to avoid trouble rather than judging his friend, which makes it easier to accept.

subtype: Approach: rehearsing a light reply to avoid a fight [Thinking]
passage:
"Lalit, pass me your science worksheet. Five minutes."
"Can't, Zubin. Sir caught two people last week with the same answers, and he said next time he's calling parents. I really don't want my Papa in the staffroom."
"He won't notice."
"He noticed Kiran's. And Kiran changed the words."
"Hmm. True. That was scary."
"I've already got enough trouble with my handwriting marks. I can't add this."
"Okay, okay. But I don't get question three."
"Question three I can explain. That's not copying. Come here."
"You're not angry with me for asking?"
"Why would I be? I just don't want to end up in the staffroom."
Zubin grinned and pulled his chair closer.

qa.q: What did Sir say he'd do next time?
How does Lalit feel while refusing?
qa.a: Calm but a bit worried about trouble, and not angry with Zubin at all.
Giving a reason about himself, so Zubin didn't feel judged, and then offering to explain question three.

qa.q: How does Zubin take the refusal?
qa.a: Zubin accepts it and grins, relieved that Lalit isn't angry with him.

grounding: A boy refuses to share answers with a reason about avoiding trouble himself, not judging his friend, which keeps things friendly.
